items.title: 'Brutal but necessary': NDIS changes to shift thousands onto states
items.description: Labor's plan to rein in NDIS growth will result in more than 160,000 people shifting off the scheme, with states expected to deliver alternative "foundational supports".

items.title: People with autism to be at centre of 160,000 NDIS removals
items.description: Minister Mark Butler announces his decision to remove more than 160,000 people from the national disability scheme over the next four years, with the timing labelled "troublesome" by autism advocates.

items.title: The proposed NDIS changes explained in five key points
items.description: Health Minister Mark Butler has unveiled sweeping cuts to the ballooning National Disability Insurance Scheme, aimed at cutting costs of the program down to $55 billion by the end of the decade.

items.title: Government ends special private health treatment for over 65s
items.description: The federal government argues the move will help re-establish fairness across the generations.

items.title: Australian billionaire's waste-to-energy plan labelled 'waste colonialism'
items.description: The controversial project would see waste burned to create energy in Fiji to reduce the country's reliance on fossil fuels, but locals and environmentalists are not happy.

items.title: ICC judges reject bid to release former Philippines president Rodrigo Duterte
items.description: Earlier hearings heard Rodrigo Duterte was allegedly responsible for thousands of deaths during his war on drugs.

items.title: Live: Several ships attacked in Strait of Hormuz as Iran calls on US to lift blockade
items.description: Three ships have been fired on in the Strait of Hormuz in recent hours, sources say, after Iran said it would not participate in peace talks until the US lifts its blockade. Follow live.

items.title: Embattled salmon industry launches advertising blitz amid calls to shut down
items.description: A new advertising campaign featuring the stories of workers adjacent to Tasmania's fish farming industry is launched amid calls for the sector to be shut down.

items.title: Passengers return to Perth Airport after police investigate unattended bag
items.description: Passengers are allowed back into Terminal 1 after an exclusion zone was established at the airport for roughly two hours.

items.title: 'Spectacularly ill-advised': Energy giants condemn gas tax
items.description: An inquiry into the taxation of gas resources has heard from proponents for a tax, who believe Australians are being robbed of their fair share of wealth from the nation's natural resources, and opponents, who argue touching tax settings would spook investors.

items.title: 101yo Bombing of Darwin veteran wants Australians to know what unfolded
items.description: At 101 years old, Bombing of Darwin survivor Terrance Byrne wants Australians to know exactly what unfolded during the World War II attack on Darwin — still the single largest foreign attack on Australian soil.

items.title: Pocock slams 'infuriating' gambling reforms as not going far enough
items.description: Former Wallaby captain turned ACT senator David Pocock argues that Anthony Albanese's proposed gambling reforms do not go far enough and calls for parliamentarians to put vested interests aside to issue a blanket ban.

items.title: 'Lost everything': New Zealand's capital cleans up as rain pushes north
items.description: Police have found the body of a man as floodwaters recede in New Zealand's capital and the clean-up begins.

items.title: 'I'm the worst cook in the house': How households make mealtimes easier
items.description: From share houses to solo living, this is how three households manage the cooking differently.

items.title: The Michael Jackson biopic is as generic as its subject was singular
items.description: Spanning from the Jackson 5's 1960s discovery through to the height of his fame in the late 80s, Michael skates over the more challenging aspects of the King of Pop.

items.title: 'It's been horrible': Your experiences with family estrangement
items.description: Our recent stories about the grief of family estrangement resonated strongly. Here's how some Australians have been affected by it.

items.title: Iran's meme factory is using 'the weapons of their enemy' to embarrass Trump
items.description: AI-generated Lego memes criticising the conflict in the Middle East and mocking Donald Trump are attracting a large audience online as a new front opens in the Iran war.

items.title: US senator 'tremendously concerned' after navy moves assets from Pacific
items.description: The US's Indo-Pacific commander praises work to upgrade Australia's AUKUS base, but says he needs more naval firepower in the region as China rapidly expands its military.

items.title: Gaza conditions 'catastrophic' as report finds $US71b needed to rebuild
items.description: More than $US71 billion will be needed over the next 10 years for recovery and reconstruction in Gaza, according to a new report by the European Union and the United Nations.

items.title: Case dropped against actor accused of 'breaking the girl code'
items.description: The actor was accused of grabbing the breast of a staffer at Parliament House in Melbourne during a pro-Palestine demonstration two years ago.

items.title: Tim Picton's accused killer pleads guilty over separate assault
items.description: A man who allegedly killed Labor identity Tim Picton in Perth admits assaulting another man in Kalamunda just days earlier.

items.title: How young boys helped Australians wage guerilla war against Japan in Timor
items.description: Incredible bonds were formed between Australian commandos and Timorese boys during World War II. The White Australia policy meant they had to say goodbye when the Anzacs departed.

items.title: Vandalised war memorial soldier repaired in time for Anzac Day
items.description: A Laurieton stonemason rushed to the task of repairing a vandalised marble rifle on a NSW Mid North Coast war memorial.

items.title: Police 'not fully prepared' for violent scene they were called to, NT inquest hears
items.description: An inquest hears evidence from a senior police officer who ran into a room to disarm a mother who was self-harming inside a Darwin crisis accommodation facility, describing the incident as "one of the worst days" of her policing career.

items.title: Travel giant's $240m overcharging scandal balloons to claims of fake agreements
items.description: Brisbane-based Corporate Travel Management has detailed a laundry list of concerns about a ballooning scandal, including reliance on potentially fake documents.
